_comment: THE WINDOW-CURRENCY RULE: when a rate-limit window reading from claudemon's
GET /usage/report may be USED, and what a reader must answer when it may not.
The rule, stated once:
A window reading is usable ONLY IF resets_at is present AND resets_at is
strictly greater than now AT THE MOMENT OF THE DECISION. A reading that
fails that test yields UNKNOWN for that window - never a percentage, never
a remaining capacity, never a time-to-reset.
is_current on the wire is a DISPLAY HINT and is never the decision input.
The daemon computes it at generated_at (usage_report.rs against the same now
that stamps generated_at), so it is correct in the response and becomes a lie
the moment a client caches or polls the document - which is exactly what a
routing engine does. Every case below therefore carries the wire's own
is_current, and the expected verdict is derived from resets_at vs now instead:
the case named 'the wire still says is_current true and the reset has since
passed' is the one that fails if a reader ever trusts the hint.
WHY THIS FIXTURE EXISTS. Live on 2026-08-30 the daemon served codex's 5h
window as used_percent ok 67.0 against a resets_at 1 day 23 hours in the
PAST. The percentage is real history and a false present, and both arms of
the routing spec's initial mode rule read it wrong in opposite directions:
SPEND_DOWN arm - 'time_to_reset < 90 minutes' is TRIVIALLY TRUE on a
negative number, so a literal implementation spends down premium
allowance against a window that closed two days ago.
CONSERVE arm - 'remaining capacity' reads 33% from a window that has in
fact rolled over to ~100%, so the fleet conserves for no reason. That one
is self-reinforcing: conserving slows the arrival of a fresh reading,
which keeps the stale one authoritative.
Both owners implement the same currency test and disagree deliberately about
what they do with a CURRENT reading, which is why only the currency verdict
is pinned here:
apps/desktop/.../services/keepWarmLogic.ts fiveHourWindowFromReport (TS)
deliberately DISCARDS the percentage - windowActive() treats any pct above
zero as a live window, so forwarding a stale 67% would suppress codex
warming permanently. Its three returns are exactly this fixture's three
verdicts: {five_hour_resets_at} = current, {} = rolled-over, null =
unreadable.
services/hub/internal/limits/window.go (Go) is the ROUTING reader and
needs the percentage, so it answers the wider question - the same currency
test, returning the reading plus its provenance when current and an
explicit unreadable/rolled-over reason when not.
usedPercent and secondsToReset are pinned as null on every non-current case
on purpose. 'UNKNOWN' has to mean no number at all; a reader that answered
0% and no reset would satisfy 'it refused' while handing a router a figure.
THE BLOCK REGISTRY. Every array-of-objects block in this file must be
declared here and everything here must be a block - closure in both
directions. Held by cmd/brain/corpusvocab_test.go and
apps/desktop/src/main/services/contractsVocabulary.test.ts.

cases.why: One rate-limit window reading from GET /usage/report, the instant a decision is being made about it, and whether that reading may be used - plus, when it may not, which of the two ways it failed.

rolledOverReasons.reset-time-has-passed: resets_at is present and is strictly before now, so the window this reading describes has closed. A DEFINITE answer: no window from this reading is running.
rolledOverReasons.reset-time-equals-now: resets_at is exactly now. The comparison is strictly greater-than, which is the boundary services/claudemon/src/providers/codex_usage.rs already pins as not-current, so the two sides cannot disagree by one second.

unreadableReasons.no-reset-time-reported: The source reported no resets_at. A percentage alone cannot say WHICH window it describes, which is why the daemon leaves is_current null here too - so this is genuinely unknown rather than definitely lapsed.
unreadableReasons.no-window-reading-at-all: There is no window object for this provider/account/window at all. Nothing to judge; ask a different source.

cases.name: a live 5h window with room left
cases.why: The claude default login exactly as the live daemon served it on 2026-08-30. A future resets_at is the only thing that makes a percentage usable, and window_minutes null is normal for Anthropic - it must not be mistaken for an unreadable window.

cases.name: a genuine zero on an open window is an answer, not an absence
cases.why: codex's 7d window, live on 2026-08-30. Measured.ok carries a real zero and a reader that treats 0 as missing turns a healthy provider into an unknown one - the exact collapse the three-state scalar exists to prevent.

cases.name: the live codex 5h reading, two days after its window closed
cases.why: The live row this whole fixture exists for, verbatim: used 67.0, resets_at 1787953526, window_minutes 300, observed on 2026-08-30. Signed, time_to_reset is -170569 seconds. A router that reads it gets 33% remaining from a window that has actually reset to about 100%, and a 'reset in under 90 minutes' arm that is trivially true.

cases.name: a dead window whose stale percentage also passes the spend-down capacity test
cases.why: The sharper half of the same defect. Both spend-down preconditions appear satisfied at once - remaining reads 80% and time_to_reset is -3600, which is under 90 minutes on any unsigned or unguarded comparison - so a literal implementation promotes every role against a window that closed an hour ago.

cases.name: the wire still says is_current true and the reset has since passed
cases.why: THE case that fails if a reader trusts the hint. is_current was true when the document was generated and the document was then cached for one second; currency has to be decided against the caller's own clock, so the wire's answer and the correct answer disagree here by construction.

cases.name: one second before the reset
cases.why: The open side of the boundary. Same reading as the live codex row, judged one second earlier: it was a true 67% then, which is why the percentage is only ever wrong relative to a clock.

cases.name: resets_at exactly equals now
cases.why: The closed side of the same boundary, one second later. codex_usage.rs's is_current already answers false at exactly the reset (resets_at > now, strictly), so pinning it here is what stops a >= creeping into either reader and disagreeing with the daemon by one second.

cases.name: a percentage the source could not read, on a window that is still open

used_percent.reason: the most recent rollout carrying rate limits did not include this window

cases.why: Currency and readability are separate axes and both readers must keep them apart. The window IS the one running - so a time-to-reset is knowable and spend-down may reason about it - while the percentage is not, so no capacity figure may be invented for it.

cases.name: a percentage with no reset time at all
cases.why: The reading that most looks usable and is not. A number with no window attached cannot say which window it describes, so it must answer UNKNOWN - never '67% and no reset', and never the '0% and no reset' a reader that zero-fills the missing half would produce.

cases.name: copilot: a window nobody can ever report

used_percent.reason: GitHub exposes no local quota record, and copilot_internal/v2/token answers 403 to a gh OAuth token (probed live against copilot CLI v1.0.81)

cases.why: unavailable is a permanent structural answer where unknown is a retryable one, and the currency test cannot tell them apart - both give no reset time, so both are unreadable HERE. Keeping the distinction alive is the reading's job, not the currency guard's; what matters is that neither yields a capacity.

cases.name: no window object at all
cases.why: A provider or account the document does not carry a window for. Distinct from a window that reports nothing readable, and distinct again from one that has lapsed: nothing here is even a claim, so it can never be rendered as a lapsed window either.
